title: trias pulvinata
intro: Trias pulvinata, commonly known as the Pulvina or False Pulvina, is a climbing plant species in the family Convolvulaceae, native to tropical regions of Central and South America. This plant has been traditionally used to treat various health issues, including fever, cough, and respiratory problems, due to its health benefits of reducing inflammation and acting as an expectorant. The therapeutic actions of Trias pulvinata include its sedative, anti-inflammatory, and antimicrobial properties, which can help to calm the nervous system and prevent infections. The bioactive constituents of this plant include flavonoids, alkaloids, and phenolic compounds, such as kaempferol and quercetin, which contribute to its medicinal properties.
